title: India's Equity Mutual Fund Returns: A 30-Year Perspective
description: Indian equity mutual funds have delivered an average return of 13% annually over the last three decades, highlighting their potential for long-term wealth cre.

faq.q: Are past returns indicative of future performance?
faq.a: No, past performance of a mutual fund is not a guarantee or indicator of future returns. Market conditions, economic factors, and fund management strategies can change, impacting future outcomes.

faq.q: What is rupee cost averaging in SIPs?
faq.a: Rupee cost averaging is a strategy where you invest a fixed amount regularly. This means you buy more units when prices are low and fewer units when prices are high, averaging out your purchase cost over time and potentially reducing risk.

faq.q: How are equity mutual fund gains taxed in India?
faq.a: Long-term Capital Gains (LTCG) from equity mutual funds (held for over 1 year) are taxed at 10% on gains exceeding ₹1 lakh in a financial year, without indexation benefit. Short-term Capital Gains (STCG) are taxed at 15%.

faq.q: Should NRIs invest in Indian equity mutual funds?
faq.a: Yes, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) can invest in Indian equity mutual funds. It offers them an opportunity to participate in India's growth story. However, they need to adhere to specific regulatory guidelines and KYC requirements.

faq.q: What is the ideal investment horizon for equity mutual funds?
faq.a: For equity mutual funds, an ideal investment horizon is typically 5-7 years or more. This allows your investments enough time to ride out market volatility and benefit from the power of compounding.

faq.q: How can I choose the right equity mutual fund?
faq.a: Consider factors like the fund's investment objective, fund manager's experience, expense ratio, past performance (while understanding its limitations), and your own risk tolerance and financial goals. Consulting a Certified Financial Planner can also be beneficial.
